_layer: MAIN DOCUMENTED / HOUSING PORTABLE BENEFITS & RESIDUAL RENT FORMULAS
_status: DRAFT SLICE — Part B only. Every claim backed by a Part A quote already extracted in this session. Do not promote without adjudication.
_note: Covers the major provincial residual and portable housing benefits that name CMHC AMR/MMR or a residual income percentage. Isolated nodes allowed. Soft/financing edges excluded.

reports.title: CMHC Rental Market Survey (Average and Median Market Rents)
reports.description: Annual survey of the primary rental market (privately initiated structures with ≥3 units). Produces both average rent (AMR) and median rent (MMR / rent_median) series used by multiple provincial residual formulas.
reports.cadence_note: Conducted each October; results published in the following months.

reports.title: Canada-Ontario Housing Benefit (portable housing benefit)
reports.publisher: Ontario Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing / Ministry of Finance
reports.description: Portable residual benefit under the National Housing Strategy. Formula set in O. Reg. 367/11.

reports.title: Manitoba Rent Assist
reports.description: Residual benefit calculated against CMHC Median Market Rent. Separate treatment for EIA and non-EIA recipients.

reports.title: Alberta Rent Assistance Benefit (RAB) / Canada-Alberta Housing Benefit
reports.publisher: Alberta Assisted Living and Social Services / Housing management bodies
reports.description: Long-term rent subsidy jointly funded under the National Housing Strategy. Residual calculation now based on 30% of total household income (including AISH) effective October 2025.

reports.title: British Columbia Shelter Aid for Elderly Renters (SAFER)
reports.description: Residual benefit for seniors. Formula set in the Shelter Aid for Elderly Renters Regulation.

reports.title: British Columbia Rental Assistance Program (RAP)
reports.description: Residual benefit for low-income families with dependent children. Uses 30% of gross household income residual against maximum rent ceilings.

reports.title: Programme de supplément au loyer Québec (PSLQ)
reports.description: Residual rent set at 25% of total household income under the Règlement sur les conditions de location des logements à loyer modique.

reports.title: Canada-Nova Scotia Targeted Housing Benefit
reports.description: Portable residual benefit. Formula: actual rent (capped at CMHC AMR) minus 30% of total household income. Eligibility threshold 40% of income on AMR.

reports.title: New Brunswick Rent Supplement Program
reports.description: Rent reduced to 30% of adjusted household income; program covers the difference up to market rent.

reports.title: Saskatchewan Housing Benefit
reports.description: Fixed monthly top-up under the National Housing Strategy based on shelter-cost-to-income ratio (≥35%). Co-funded federal-provincial.

dependencies.basis: O. Reg. 367/11 (Housing Services Act, 2011): formula 80% AMR – [(AFNI × 0.30)/12]. AMR defined as CMHC average market rent data posted on the Ministry website, sourced from the annual Rental Market Survey.

Manitoba Rent Assist program materials: benefits calculated as difference between 80% of Median Market Rent and 30% of net household income. Explicit statement that Median Market Rent is established by the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation.

Nova Scotia 2024 program update: benefit calculated as actual rent (capped at average monthly rent for the area) minus 30% of total household income. Explicitly adopts CMHC household income levels and average market rents.

Shelter Aid for Elderly Renters Regulation s. 5: rent gap = lesser of rent or maximum rent minus 30% of eligible renter’s income; benefit is 90% of gap (or sliding percentage). Maximum rents set administratively; base income tied to OAS+GIS+provincial supplement.

Programme de supplément au loyer Québec: household pays 25% of total income (calculated under Règlement sur les conditions de location des logements à loyer modique). Loyers médians du marché adjusted jointly by SHQ and SCHL from SCHL survey data.

Alberta Rent Assistance Benefit under Canada-Alberta Housing Benefit (NHS). Effective October 2025: rent / benefit based on 30% of total household income, including AISH and Income Support. Amount previously described as calculated from household income and local market rent.
New Brunswick Rent Supplement Program: tenant rent reduced to 30% of adjusted household income; program funds the difference to market rent.

Saskatchewan Housing Benefit (NHS cost-shared): fixed monthly amounts determined by household size and whether shelter costs equal 35–45% or >45% of before-tax income. Eligibility requires ≥35% of income spent on shelter.
dependencies.evidence_url: Saskatchewan Housing Corporation fact sheets (2026 rates)

_notes: CMHC Rental Market Survey is the single most frequently named external statistical input across residual housing benefits.
AMR (mean) vs MMR (median) distinction is documented: Ontario/Nova Scotia use average; Manitoba uses median. Same underlying survey.
Alberta’s October 2025 change fully includes AISH in the 30% residual calculation — relevant to earlier disability-benefit extractions.
Quebec uses a lower residual (25%) than the common 30% residual used elsewhere.
No soft or financing edges included. Isolated residual nodes retained where the statute does not name an external series.
